description: Google-Only Sign-In & Public Schedule — retire email/password + self-serve signup in favor of Supabase Google OAuth, make the room schedule publicly viewable as the landing page, and defer the sign-in prompt to the moment a signed-out visitor tries to create a booking (preserving their selected room/date/time across the login round-trip). Reverses the prior 'entire app requires auth' rule for the schedule only; booking/admin/member routes stay gated. Source: tasks/prd-google-auth-public-schedule.md.

userStories.title: Enable Google OAuth provider in Supabase config
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Supabase Google provider enabled and wired to environment secrets so the app can authenticate users via Google.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/config.toml has an [auth.external.google] block with enabled = true, client_id = "env(SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)", and secret = "env(SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_GOOGLE_SECRET)"
skip_nonce_check = true is set in the [auth.external.google] block (required for local Google sign-in per the config comments)
site_url / additional_redirect_urls in config.toml include the local dev callback http://127.0.0.1:3000/auth/callback plus a placeholder/production URL entry
Create .env.example (if absent) documenting SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_GOOGLE_SECRET; no real secret values are committed
DEPLOYMENT.md documents the Google Cloud OAuth consent-screen/credentials setup and the Supabase dashboard Google-provider fields needed in production
No Google Workspace domain restriction is configured — any Google account may sign in
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add the OAuth callback route
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a server route that exchanges the OAuth code for a session so Google sign-in completes and returns the user to where they started.
acceptanceCriteria: app/auth/callback/route.ts reads the code query param and calls supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession(code) using the server client from lib/supabase/server.ts
On success it redirects to the next query param when present, otherwise to /schedule
The next param is validated to be a relative path only (starts with '/', not '//' or a scheme) — absolute/off-site URLs are rejected and fall back to /schedule
On error it redirects to /login?error=<message>
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Grant public (anon) read access to the schedule data
userStories.description: As a developer, I need unauthenticated visitors to read the schedule view and room list so the public schedule can render, without exposing member identity or notes.
acceptanceCriteria: A new timestamped migration in supabase/migrations grants SELECT on public.bookings_schedule to the anon role
The migration grants anon read of rooms: add an RLS policy allowing anon SELECT on rooms and 'grant select on rooms to anon'
No anon access is granted to base bookings, profiles, favorite_rooms, or notifications — identity, notes, and reject reasons stay unreadable to anon
Migration applies cleanly via 'supabase db reset' (or equivalent) with no errors
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Replace the login page with Continue with Google
userStories.description: As a member, I want to sign in with one Google button instead of entering an email and password.
acceptanceCriteria: app/login/page.tsx renders a single 'Continue with Google' button (no email/password fields) and reads optional next and error values from searchParams

A server action calls supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'google', options: { redirectTo } }) where redirectTo points at /auth/callback and carries the next param through, then redirects to the returned data.url
The old email/password login action in app/login/actions.ts is removed/replaced
app/signup/ (page + action) is deleted and /signup no longer resolves to a signup form (404 or redirect to /login)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (button renders; clicking it initiates Google OAuth — a Google consent screen or the expected local-dev redirect appears)

userStories.title: Make the schedule publicly viewable in middleware
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to open the app and see the schedule without being redirected to a login screen.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/supabase/middleware.ts allows unauthenticated access to the schedule/home, /login, and /auth/callback via an explicit public path-prefix allowlist (and no longer references /signup)
All booking, admin, availability-create, notification, and other member routes still redirect unauthenticated users to /login with a next param capturing the attempted path
A signed-in user visiting /login is still redirected away to the schedule
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (logged out: opening the app shows the schedule with no redirect to login; opening a booking route redirects to login)

userStories.title: Schedule is the landing page and renders for signed-out users
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the schedule to be the first thing I see, with a clear way to sign in, whether or not I am logged in.
acceptanceCriteria: Visiting / shows the schedule (redirect / to /schedule, or serve the schedule at root)
The schedule page and its app shell render without error when there is no authenticated user (favorites and any user-specific UI degrade gracefully on user === null — no crash)
When signed out, the app shell shows a 'Sign in' link (to /login) where the account menu normally sits; when signed in, the account menu appears as before
The schedule shows room, date, time, status, and service/purpose label only — no member names, notes, or reject reasons for any viewer
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (logged-out schedule shows the Sign in affordance; logged-in schedule shows the account menu)

userStories.title: Booking creation prompts sign-in and preserves the selected slot
userStories.description: As a signed-out visitor, when I try to book a slot I want to be asked to sign in and then land back on the booking form with my chosen room/date/time still selected.
acceptanceCriteria: When a signed-out user triggers booking creation (drag-to-create, a Book action, or navigating to /bookings/new) they are sent to /login?next=<booking-form-url> where the booking-form URL encodes the selected room, date, start, and end
The booking form at /bookings/new reads and applies room/date/start/end query params to pre-fill the form (add support if not already present)
After completing Google sign-in the user lands on /bookings/new with room/date/start/end pre-filled from those params
A signed-in user's booking flow is unchanged (no extra login prompt)
The 5-pending-cap, shared conflict-check, and status lifecycle behavior are unaffected
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (logged out: select a slot, tap Book, complete Google login, and return to the booking form with the slot preserved)

userStories.title: Confirm admin access under Google-only auth
userStories.description: As an admin, I want my elevated access to keep working after switching to Google sign-in, with admin still granted manually in the database.
acceptanceCriteria: A profile row is created for first-time Google sign-ins (the existing profile_on_signup_trigger fires for OAuth users; display_name is populated from Google metadata where available, else falls back to email)
New profiles default to role = 'member' and there is no self-serve path to admin
DEPLOYMENT.md documents the exact SQL/step to grant admin by manually setting profiles.role = 'admin'
Admin-only routes/actions remain gated on role = 'admin' and are unreachable by members or anon (middleware/route guards still hold)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill (a member Google account cannot open admin routes; a DB-flagged admin can)

userStories.title: Update project docs to reflect public schedule + Google-only auth
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the canonical docs to match the new auth model so future work does not re-gate the schedule or re-add password login.
acceptanceCriteria: CLAUDE.md is updated: the 'entire app requires authentication' rule is amended to 'the schedule is public; booking and all member/admin actions require Google sign-in'
tasks/prd-gac-reservations-v1.md gets a note pointing to tasks/prd-google-auth-public-schedule.md as the superseding source for auth + schedule visibility
Any reference to email/password signup/login in the docs is corrected to Google-only
Typecheck passes
